report: The patient has a one-month pruritic, painful periorbital eruption with scaly, crusted pink plaques and a history of lupus nephritis/ITP. Left upper eyelid biopsy shows vacuolar interface dermatitis with follicular involvement and epidermal atrophy, classic for cutaneous lupus erythematosus, refuting drug-induced eruption and seborrheic dermatitis. DIF/autoantibody testing unavailable, but clinical, autoimmune, and biopsy findings make cutaneous lupus erythematosus the most likely diagnosis.
